figmaExecutionNotes: Keep the top trust bar visible and sticky across the page only if implemented as a global banner component; otherwise preserve it directly under hero as a high-priority proof strip.
Use a light theme throughout with brand-accent CTAs and white feature cards over very light grey section breaks.
Do not add pricing, testimonials, news, or form sections because they are not supported by the provided content.
Mobile should stack sections vertically, collapse feature grids to single column, and keep CTAs full-width stacked with primary first.
Ensure the full page is designed as a scrollable landing page, not a hero-only composition.
Avoid nested grids inside feature sections; use simple card grids or split rows for readability.
Use consistent card spacing, section headings, and content hierarchy so the page feels like one system, not separate modules.
Because the trust strategy says logos are the dominant signal, reserve the strongest visual weight after hero for the trust bar and keep it above all feature content.

heroStrategy.headline: Deliver Exceptional Customer Support with Zoho Desk
heroStrategy.subheadline: Streamline customer service, manage tickets efficiently, and deliver seamless support experiences across every channel.
heroStrategy.designNote: Use an unexpected split hero with the media block on the left as a layered product showcase: one main dashboard mockup, one smaller floating ticket-routing panel, plus a thin omnichannel icon strip and trust marquee. Keep the text on the right in a clean editorial stack with a large 60px+ H1, orange primary CTA, and indigo secondary accents. Background should be a soft warm-white mesh gradient with subtle grid lines and low-opacity orbit shapes for depth. No dark hero, but introduce a later dark section for contrast. Overall feel: bright, organized, credible SaaS marketplace landing page with strong proof-first hierarchy.

repetitionBreakers: Start with a split hero, then switch to a compact logo proof strip to avoid repeating the same content-heavy pattern.
Use a text-and-preview how-it-works section next, so the page changes from broad promise to operational clarity.
Alternate product sections between split-panel storytelling and spotlight-plus-grid to keep long feature content from becoming visually flat.
Place the strongest proof immediately after the workflow explanation, then move into feature depth before pricing.
End with a centered pricing card followed by a testimonial carousel and a final lead form, so the close feels progressively more persuasive.
blueprint.pageTitle: Zoho Desk Customer Support Software | Streamline Tickets, Omnichannel Service & AI
blueprint.metaDescription: Deliver faster, smarter customer support with Zoho Desk. Manage tickets, support every channel, use AI assistance, and streamline workflows for your team.

sections.backgroundTreatment: warm white-to-cream gradient with subtle dashboard panel overlays and orange-indigo accent chips
sections.designNote: Make the hero content-first but visually dynamic. Headline should answer what this is: Zoho Desk customer support software. Subheadline should answer who it is for: businesses and support teams. CTA must be the single approved text, Get started, styled as solid accent at full opacity. Right side should show a polished help desk dashboard mockup with inbox, ticket routing, AI suggestions, and omnichannel cards.

Use a compact logo-style trust block immediately after the hero. Because the input does not include 3-6 recognizable customer logos, convert proof into a clean metrics-led trust strip featuring Trusted by 100,000+ Businesses Globally, award badge, and support/reliability chips. Keep it visually light and highly scannable.

featurePresentation.primaryFeatureTitle: How it works in under 60 seconds

sections.designNote: Reframe the first product block as a 3-step workflow section instead of a generic feature dump: 1) Capture tickets across channels, 2) Route and automate with workflows, 3) Resolve faster with AI and collaboration. Use a left text / right visual split with numbered steps and a preview panel. Then follow with alternating product blocks: one spotlighting omnichannel support and ticket management, another spotlighting Zia AI and workflow automation. Keep each block visually distinct using alternating panel direction and different card densities.

Treat this as a concise credibility-and-confidence section, not a generic vendor pitch. Use a 2-column or 3-column grid with short support-ops benefits, implementation ease, and secure cloud reliability. Maintain a lighter, warmer background to break from the previous section and avoid adjacent repetition.

Present pricing as a focused conversion card with an included-features checklist. Keep the section minimal and decisive. CTA text must remain Get started. Avoid comparison tables because the page already has long product content and warm traffic benefits from a clearer single-path close.

Use a testimonial carousel or compact grid because there are 5 testimonials. Make this section credibility-forward, with strong quote hierarchy and role/company metadata. Visually distinct from pricing via a cooler neutral background and softer framing.

End with a clean centered lead form or conversion card. Since the CTA rule is strict, the primary button must say Get started and be full-width on mobile. Keep the field count low and pair with a final reassurance line about secure cloud setup and quick onboarding.

Do not use marquee motion. If used at all, this should be a static horizontal logo strip or a small media badge row. Since the input lacks real press/logo assets, this can be omitted or reduced to a subtle trust footer treatment.

blueprint.designPersonality: Professional, organized, and reassuring with a modern support-ops feel. The page should feel like a premium B2B marketplace landing page: bright, trustworthy, structured, and conversion-focused, with logos and customer proof as the strongest trust signal.
blueprint.imageryDirection: Use clean SaaS UI visuals: ticket inbox, omnichannel message cards, AI suggestion panels, workflow routing chips, and integration tiles. Favor white cards, soft shadows, and small orange-indigo highlights. Proof area should prioritize a logo marquee and customer count stat over decorative photography.

referenceMap.heroPattern: Single-column, full-width banner hero with brand logo at top, large centered headline, concise supporting copy, and a short bullet/value-prop list beneath. No split media treatment in the reference; emphasis is text-first with strong top-weighted hierarchy.
referenceMap.sectionRhythm: Hero leads into a lead-capture form block, then compact content sections with clear vertical separation. Layout favors stacked sections, moderate-to-generous whitespace, and repeated headline-plus-supporting-copy patterns over dense multi-column grids.
referenceMap.cardStyle: Primarily simple, utilitarian content blocks rather than decorative cards. Form container acts like a card with a bordered/boxed feel; product sections read as clean text modules with optional icon-led feature rows.
referenceMap.ctaPattern: Primary CTA is prominent and action-oriented in the hero; secondary CTA is present but visually subordinate. Additional conversion happens through a dedicated form section instead of repeated button clusters throughout the page.
referenceMap.pricingPattern: No visible pricing pattern in the reference structure.
referenceMap.footerMode: Footer is not present in the provided reference extract, so no reusable footer pattern can be inferred.
referenceMap.mediaPattern: Minimal media usage in the captured section. Brand logo appears in the hero; no dominant product imagery, gallery, or embedded video pattern is evident. Visual communication is mostly typographic.
referenceMap.productSectionPattern: Long-form, sequential product storytelling with repeated section headline, short description, then feature list. Best suited for stacked feature grids or 2-column feature groupings; supports progressive disclosure through multiple themed sections.
referenceMap.formPattern: Dedicated lead-generation form immediately after hero, presented as a focused conversion block with a strong heading and multiple fields. Form is visually separated from content and designed as the primary response action.
referenceMap.animationStyle: Static, presentation-style layout with no clear motion system exposed in the reference HTML.

designStrategy.reasoning: This is a single-product lead-gen landing page for Zoho Desk, and the strongest conversion path is to clearly explain the product, build trust quickly, and push toward trial or expert contact. Because the audience is warm and evaluating support software, the page should be product-led with a logos-first trust strategy, since the brief explicitly says visitors trust logos most. The design should stay light, clean, and efficient, with a centered hero that emphasizes the message and CTAs rather than complex visuals. Section flow should move from proof to benefits, AI capability, integrations, customization, pricing inclusions, and testimonials, giving both product clarity and conversion reassurance without overwhelming the user.
